title: fix(macos): stop push-to-talk capture when its hold ends
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes microphone capture starting after a push-to-talk hold has ended, right Option remaining active when left Option is still held, and stale voice transitions acquiring or releasing a newer session's resources.

## User Impact

- Releasing physical right Option ends the hold even while left Option remains down. Disabling push-to-talk cancels pending or active capture.
- Ordinary release retains the existing 1.5-second Speech drain and send; forced teardown cancels without forwarding.
- Talk suppresses push-to-talk through admission and audio shutdown. Overlay dismissal cannot release another voice owner's wake pause.
- A fresh hold can adopt visible text without forwarding the replaced capture twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The AppState-owned graph binds PTT, Wake, Talk, session coordination, overlay actions, and acquired cleanup collaborators at construction. Hotkey invalidation is synchronous on MainActor; asynchronous startup and cleanup remain bound to the originating hold, lifecycle, owner, and acknowledged wake pause. Shared accessors project the production graph rather than creating disconnected owners.

The October 1 refresh preserves the original PR ancestry and incorporates main `55bbbf9ddcad46c7746ef8c66c73c5c71197406f`. It retains main's consolidated session source and audio shutdown/reconfiguration checks, routes new overlay-edit and Talk callbacks through the injected owner graph, and uses the current ear-boost state instead of removed helper methods. The lifecycle test now verifies edited overlay text reaches the owning coordinator and send action. Documentation describes the visible overlay lifetime without the obsolete helper reference.

No configuration, defaults, persistence, schema, protocol, or dependency changes. Microphone-selection semantics are unchanged; PCM append is not moved onto MainActor.

## Evidence

### October 1 candidate

Head: `7e036e0369761a3f5ee899797868881a1dc9364c`. The merge commit retains original PR head `f383129f85d9c8e6a289cb11731ee163629eb802` as a parent; its follow-up commit changes test argument formatting only.

- Swift frontend parsing passed all 20 changed Swift files. This is syntax proof, not native typechecking.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.0 and strict SwiftLint 0.65.1 passed all 20 files; scoped oxfmt and whitespace checks passed. An initial SourceKit loader failure and a test-format lint failure remain failed attempts, not product findings; the final checks completed after supported process-local toolchain selection and formatting.
- Independent source review completed. Its sole P1 report assumed `voiceWakeMicID` was optional. The actual owner declares a nonoptional `String`, initializes the system default to `""`, and the existing selection resolver normalizes the empty string to the default device. The optional guard tests owner presence, not microphone selection; the report does not apply. No speculative microphone change was made.
- [October 1 CI 36862423196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36862423196) completed successfully for this head, including macOS packages, [macOS tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36862423196/job/110370100628), and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The actual logged checkout was `4f1345a25735a51e4efae5816f517f36fb9187f9`, with ordered parents `ec8df3aa0f39d505d59a49b39fea9fb04d478ac5` and `7e036e0369761a3f5ee899797868881a1dc9364c`, not a standalone head checkout. The default suite passed 2403 tests/277 suites; the separate rendered suite passed two tests/one suite and the named suite passed six tests/two suites. Complete retained test logs confirm the selected owner-lifecycle, hotkey, speech/recovery/overlay cases and AppState isolation, including edited-overlay send. This qualifies the recorded merge checkout, not signed interactive behavior. September CI is historical only; fresh review completion and final landing gates remain required.

Production versus main is +1019/-484, tests/support +679/-55, and documentation +8/-6. The retained production growth establishes concrete ownership across the existing cyclic voice graph and replaces global escape paths; it does not add a parallel Talk-start path.

### Retained native and historical evidence

[CI run 34389511457, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34389511457/attempts/1) ran on September 9 for old PR head `f383129f85d9c8e6a289cb11731ee163629eb802`. The logged checkout was `c10d6578c98c2870957c02d7550b207436f5abe3`, with ordered parents `10af9baebe45b2e123857e512ed186714ad6d1f8` and that PR head. [macos-swift tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34389511457/job/102594272037) and the CI gate passed: 15 expected named tests represented 19 cases (11 lifecycle, six speech, two hotkey), through aggregate completion and parameter admissions, not 19 individual finish records. The default suite completed 2140 tests/237 suites; AppStateIsolation completed two tests/one suite. Release build was skipped.

Earlier identical-fixture PTT/coordinator pre/post proof produced 77 passed/19 failed assertions before repair and 96 passed/zero failed afterward across 22 scenarios. Both runs separately passed 20 isolation checks. Those runs compiled whole owners against synthetic native boundaries, not copied algorithms; they belong to earlier wiring and do not prove the refreshed composition. Earlier Talk testing used a synthetic runtime, and historical SDK typechecking was compile-only with application stubs.

Earlier [CI 34345983026](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34345983026), [CI 34350899352](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34350899352), and [Periphery 34350899558](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34350899558) remain dated observations of older heads, not current qualification. The earlier unused-key-code Periphery failure was repaired, not waived.

### Limits and follow-ups

Still unproven: an identical-wiring pre-fix pair for the current graph; successful signed microphone/Speech permission flows; physical modifier delivery; rendered overlay animation; and arbitrary native Speech/Wake suspension schedules. PTT fixture admissions deny permission, so they do not establish successful capture. No signed interactive app or full native suite ran on an operator desktop, and no screenshots or recordings are claimed.

The fixtures do not prove complete quiescence or cross-suite isolation: private PTT startup/late completions, initial/dismissal-triggered Wake tasks, queued monitor registrations, and phase publications remain unjoined.

Known follow-ups remain explicit: the pre-existing Wake stop path can dismiss an overlay without a token after the last pause is released; manual-send versus PTT draft adoption remains an existing source risk; microphone selection, including unused PTT `micID`, is not certified here. The prior ClawSweeper signed-capture rank-up remains unfulfilled and is not presented as passing evidence. Fresh review completion and current native CI are required before landing; physical/signed proof is not claimed.
